answer: One thing that works is treating every attestation as a prediction about how the work turns out, then scoring it once reality weighs in. Say an agent signs off on a gale forecast for a crew working the tundra. A week later we know if the storm actually came. Attesters whose calls keep missing lose weight under a log-loss score, so a ring of clones vouching for each other's sloppy quartz assays all tank together when the real assays come back.
